name: Regional PostgreSQL authority
description: PostgreSQL is the authority for identities, rooms, session leases, allocation reservations, match tickets/proposals, durable results, statistics and leaderboard revisions. Core owns writes. Unique constraints + row locks/CAS or SERIALIZABLE retries protect invariants; plain read-then-write at READ COMMITTED is insufficient. Co-locate transactionally related room/session/queue records. Persist outbox/inbox in the same database. Connection pools, query limits, PITR backup and tested failover are required.

name: Connection and projection cache
description: Optional Redis-compatible regional cache for Socket token hashes/generations, subscriptions, presence and replaceable projections. It is not the room, ticket or session authority. Cache failure forces reauthentication/resync; Core state rebuilds projections. TTL per entry, tenant key namespace, bounded memory and eviction policy are mandatory. Session leases never depend on a cache lock.

name: Checkpoint objects and runtime journal
description: Object storage contains immutable, checksummed game checkpoints/final result blobs. A durable, fenced ordered journal holds accepted game inputs, checkpoint manifests and result/outbox intents. Media Engine writes its own session namespace; Core reads manifests for recovery. The adapter must enforce token CAS and atomic durable record boundaries; object-store eventual listing is not a manifest. Retain checkpoint/log windows long enough for declared recovery; garbage-collect orphan objects safely.

name: Live leaderboard projection
description: Optional Redis projection owned by Core. PostgreSQL holds authoritative scores and per-entry revision. Apply absolute score updates only if revision increases, never blind ZINCRBY from a redelivered event. Scores are fixed-point decimal strings; values beyond exact double precision need sortable fixed-width lexicographic members or PostgreSQL reads, not Redis double scores. Rebuild in a new namespace to a watermark and atomically switch; return freshness when lagging.

name: ClickHouse analytical history
description: ClickHouse stores session facts, cumulative sample history and settled result versions for analytical queries. Core ingestion workers project asynchronously; no fourth service is introduced. ReplacingMergeTree replacement happens during merges and is not a uniqueness constraint. Queries must explicitly select the latest record per semantic key/revision (argMax/FINAL as appropriate) before aggregating. Raw duplicate inserts must never inflate settled totals. No admission, lease, reward or live rank authority depends on ClickHouse availability.

name: Mandatory session timeline and optional media archive
technology: Durable regional append journal + private object storage
description: Every admitted session has a timestamped event archive. Core PostgreSQL owns recording policy, per-source watermarks, event index and media manifests. Core/MediaEngine append immutable event batches and checksum-verified media segments to tenant/session namespaces through a fenced durable adapter. Default event retention 30 days, optional media 7 days; preserve metadata tombstones and configured holds. ClickHouse indexes/analyses copies and is never the sole recording copy. Encryption, scoped playback URLs, storage quotas, restore drills and explicit gap/completeness states are required.
